preconditions: At least one registered user exists
Token issuance is available for authenticated write operations
business_rules: Article creation, reading, updating, and deletion are in application scope
Article write operations use the custom API
Only the owning author should be able to edit or delete an article
Successful article updates should be durable and observable through later reads
Successful article deletion should remove the article from active detail and list availability
input_constraints: Create payload includes article.title, article.description, and article.body
Update target is identified by article slug
Update payload may include changed article fields
Post-update verification uses the current article slug for subsequent reads
Post-delete verification uses the deleted article slug and relevant article list filters
Exact maximum lengths, whitespace handling, and tag validation are not defined by the local fixture
error_conditions: Unauthenticated article update or deletion is rejected
Non-owner article update or deletion is rejected or otherwise forbidden
Invalid create or update payload is rejected
A successful update that is not reflected by a later read violates lifecycle persistence
Deleted article retrieval should not return an active article
A deleted article remaining visible in article lists violates deletion observability

conditions: request attempts to create an article
expected_actions: Reject unauthenticated create attempts
Allow create processing only for authenticated users
requirement_items.notes: Evidence: README.md:31 and features.md:9 confirm CRUD articles; features.md:7 confirms JWT authentication. Official endpoint docs mark article creation as authenticated.

requirement_items.description: An authenticated author can create an article with valid article data.
expected_actions: Persist the article
Associate the article with the authenticated author
Return the created article representation
requirement_items.notes: Evidence: local docs confirm article creation and official endpoint docs define POST /api/articles. Exact success status is official-spec dependent and should be verified in the target implementation.

requirement_items.description: Created article responses include the article identity, content, metadata, and author information needed for later reads.
expected_actions: Return a slug that identifies the article
Return the saved article content
Return author metadata
requirement_items.notes: Official response format defines article object fields. Local fixture only confirms article publishing and CRUD scope, not exact response fields.

requirement_items.description: Creating an article with missing or invalid required article fields is rejected.
expected_actions: Do not persist the article
Return a validation error response
requirement_items.notes: Required field validation is inferred from the official create payload and is not specified by the local fixture. Whitespace-only handling is an open implementation question.

requirement_items.description: The owning author can edit an existing article.
conditions: authenticated user is the article author
expected_actions: Apply supplied changes to the existing article
Return the updated article representation
Keep the article associated with the original author
requirement_items.notes: Evidence: README.md:31 and features.md:9 confirm article updating. Official endpoint docs define PUT /api/articles/{slug}; owner-only behavior should be verified against the implementation.

requirement_items.description: Article updates preserve unchanged article fields unless the request supplies a replacement value.
expected_actions: Change only fields included in the update payload
Preserve omitted fields
requirement_items.notes: Official API describes updating article fields, but the local fixture does not specify partial-update semantics. Treat this as a review point if the target backend differs.

requirement_items.description: Article edit attempts by unauthenticated users or non-owners are rejected.
conditions: requester is not the owning author
expected_actions: Do not modify the article
Return an unauthorized or forbidden error response
requirement_items.notes: Authentication is confirmed by official article endpoint docs. Non-owner rejection is an expected ownership rule for edit/delete operations and should be reviewed because local high-level docs do not state it explicitly.

requirement_items.description: The owning author can delete an existing article.
conditions: authenticated user is the article author
expected_actions: Remove the article from active availability
Return a successful deletion response
requirement_items.notes: Evidence: README.md:31 and features.md:9 confirm article deletion. Official endpoint docs define DELETE /api/articles/{slug}.

requirement_items.description: After an article is deleted, later retrieval of that article does not return it as an active article.
expected_actions: Do not return the deleted article as an active article
Return a not-found or equivalent unavailable response
requirement_items.notes: Deletion is confirmed in local scope. Exact post-delete status and body are not defined by the local fixture.

requirement_items.description: Article delete attempts by unauthenticated users or non-owners are rejected.
conditions: requester is not the owning author
expected_actions: Do not delete the article
Return an unauthorized or forbidden error response
requirement_items.notes: Authentication is confirmed by official endpoint docs. Non-owner deletion rejection is an expected ownership rule and should be confirmed against the target implementation.

requirement_items.description: After an article is successfully updated, later reads of that article return the persisted updated values.
data_ranges: valid update payload changing at least one persisted field
subsequent GET by current article slug
expected_actions: Persist the supplied article changes beyond the update response
Return the updated article values on a subsequent detail read
Preserve unchanged fields according to the update semantics
Expose an updated timestamp or equivalent updated metadata when supported
requirement_items.notes: Evidence: README.md:31 and features.md:9 confirm article updating and reading. This requirement makes update persistence explicit for AutoTestDesign. If title changes cause slug regeneration, the target implementation should confirm whether subsequent reads use the old slug or the returned current slug.

requirement_items.description: After an article is successfully deleted, the deleted article is no longer observable as an active article through detail or article list reads.
data_ranges: tag-filtered list when the deleted article had tags
favorited-filtered list when the deleted article had favorites
conditions: GET /api/articles is requested afterward with filters that would have included the article before deletion
expected_actions: Do not return the deleted article from detail lookup
Do not include the deleted article in global article lists
Do not include the deleted article in filtered article lists
Keep unrelated active articles visible
requirement_items.notes: Evidence: README.md:31 confirms article deletion and reading; README.md:32 and features.md:11 confirm paginated article lists. Exact not-found status, response body, and list ordering are not defined by the local fixture and should be reviewed against the target backend.
